# Onboarding guide: psf/requests

## What this project is
`Requests` is an intuitive Python HTTP client library designed around the principle of "HTTP for Humans™". It provides a high-level API for common HTTP operations (`requests.get()`, `requests.post()`, etc.) while hiding complex protocol mechanics internally behind `urllib3`. It supports Python 3.10+ and PyPy.

# Security triage: demo_app
## Summary
The codebase contains multiple severe injection and deserialization risks that could allow remote code execution. Fix finding F5 first because it directly concatenates untrusted HTTP request parameters into a system command.

## Findings
| ID | Rule | Location | Verdict | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | py-weak-hash | app/cache.py:9 | false positive | MD5 is used exclusively to generate a cache bucket name (`hashlib.md5(url.encode())`), not for cryptographic security. | None needed (non-security use). |
| F2 | py-pickle-load | app/cache.py:14 | likely | `pickle.loads` deserialises session cookies (`cookie_value`), which leads to RCE if session cookies are forgeable/untrusted. | Use a secure serializer like `json` or sign cookies with a MA
